tex_content.html:
Corollary
[Every group is $\pi _1$ of some 2-complex] ↗ prop:attaching-cells-pi1 ↗ ex:wedge-sum-fundamental-group 1. ch1:1.28\group Fundamental Group

For every group $G$ there is a 2-dimensional cell complex $X_G$ with $\pi _1(X_G)\cong G$.

Proof

\sketch Choose a presentation $G=\langle g_\alpha \mid r_\beta \rangle . Start with $\bigvee _αS^1_α$ and attach one 2-cell for each relator. The attaching-cell proposition gives the desired fundamental group. $

□
